paper_title: New Constraints on Hidden Photons using Very High Energy Gamma-Rays from the Crab Nebula
suggested_experiment_name: Crab Nebula VHE gamma-ray hidden photon constraint (HEGRA/H.E.S.S./MAGIC/Whipple)
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing chi (dimensionless), as plotted on the y-axis of Figure 2
notes: Paper derives hidden photon (dark photon) kinetic mixing constraints from photon-hidden photon oscillations of VHE gamma-rays from the Crab Nebula (HEGRA, H.E.S.S., MAGIC, Whipple data). The combined limit converges to chi >= 0.0343 excluded, valid for masses mu <~ 1e-5 eV (coherence conditions break above this). Full exclusion curve is in Fig. 2 (mu from 1e-8 to 1e-5 eV), with the limit weakening at lower masses; only the asymptotic value 0.0343 is quoted numerically in text/table, so I encode it as a flat bound over the high-mass region (~1e-6 to 1e-5 eV) where the curve has converged. IMPORTANT caveat: the paper's stated confidence level is 68.3% (Delta chi^2 = 1), not 90% or 95%; 0.90 was entered only because the schema requires one of those two values. Not a DM haloscope search, so no local DM density assumed.
